finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches an attacker-supplied URL. The only check is a substring match for "example.io", which the attacker can satisfy with any URL, e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://example.io@127.0.0.1:8080/, or http://evil.com/example.io. Redirects are followed, so an allowed-looking host can also redirect internal. The response body is returned to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) (main.go:36), with the response body copied back to the client at main.go:38

trace.note: strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is the only validation. It is a substring check, not a parsed-host check
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, which follows redirects, with no scheme, host, or IP restrictions
the response body is streamed back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: Only the strings.Contains substring check at main.go:32. There is no URL parsing, hostname allowlist, scheme check, private/link-local IP blocking, or redirect restriction. The check is bypassable via the path, query, userinfo, or a subdomain of an attacker-owned domain.

verdict.guard_found: Only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32 (substring check, does not close). The strict hostname allowlist and no-redirect client are only in the separate /cdn handler (main.go:20-24), not /logo.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the attacker-controlled `logo` form value, main.go:32 only does a substring check that any URL containing "example.io" passes, and main.go:36 calls http.Get(raw) with the default redirect-following client and main.go:38 returns the body, so full-read SSRF holds.
